TASK PART 1 — replace the stub in shared/appointmentSort.ts with the real implementation.
The file currently holds a DELIBERATELY WRONG stub (it returns rows unchanged and reports a default of status/desc) that exists only to make the red phase meaningful. Keep the exported names and types exactly as they are — DEFAULT_APPOINTMENT_SORT, nextSort, sortIndicator, sortAppointments, AppointmentSortKey, SortDirection, AppointmentSort, SortableAppointment — and make them correct. The requirements, in EARS form:
  APT-S1: sortAppointments(rows, sort) orders by sort.key ('"'"'date'"'"' | '"'"'status'"'"') in sort.dir ('"'"'asc'"'"' | '"'"'desc'"'"').
  APT-S2: DEFAULT_APPOINTMENT_SORT is date ascending — today'"'"'s behavior, which must not change on first load.
  APT-S6: the order must be TOTAL and independent of the input arrangement. When two rows tie on the sort key, break the tie by start time ASCENDING, then by id ascending. The direction applies to the SORT KEY ONLY, never to the tie-break: within one status group appointments still read soonest-first in BOTH directions.
  APT-S7: an unparseable startAt (Date.parse gives NaN) sorts LAST in BOTH directions. This is not the same as negating the comparison — think about it carefully. An unguarded `ta - tb` returns NaN, which loses every comparison and leaves whatever order the engine started with.
  APT-S8: sortAppointments must NOT mutate the array it is given. It receives react-query'"'"'s cached data.appointments; sorting in place corrupts the cache. Return a new array.
  APT-S9: startAt may be an ISO string OR a Date object, and the two must compare correctly against each other. A string comparison is not chronological.
  APT-S3/APT-S4: nextSort(current, key) returns { key, dir: '"'"'asc'"'"' } when key is not the active key, and toggles the direction when it is. It must not mutate `current`.
  APT-S5: sortIndicator(sort, column) returns sort.dir when column IS the active sort key, and null when it is not. This is the DECISION about which header shows a caret; it lives in shared/ so it has an executable test, and the component must CALL it rather than re-deriving the comparison in JSX.
Status ordering is plain alphabetical on the status string. Do NOT use localeCompare — it is locale-dependent and would make the ordering vary by machine. Use a direct `<` / `>` comparison.
